literal: Having toiled, having hoarded, 'support we are without' they will say, guests having cherished, the sacrifice those who do not undertake.
translation: Those who do not undertake the sacrifice of cherishing guests will later lament, 'We toiled and hoarded, but now we are without support.'
modern: விருந்தினரை உபசரிக்கும் வேள்வியை செய்யாதவர்கள், பொருளை வருந்தி பாதுகாத்தும் இப்போது எந்தப் பற்றும் இல்லாமல் போனோம் என்று வருந்துவார்கள்.
explanation: This couplet warns about the regret of those who hoard wealth without sharing it. The word 'parintu' means toiling or guarding with anxious care, emphasizing the selfish effort spent on hoarding. The poet uses 'velvi' (sacrifice) to show that hospitality is as sacred and essential as a formal ritual. Those who fail to undertake this duty will eventually realize that their hoarded wealth offers no real support, lamenting that they are left destitute of true companionship.
